[...] Et comme l'éolien avait généralisé la règle F (accent récessif), seul donc l'attique a pu avoir la règle G'. [p. 90] C'est ainsi que, dans le dialecte de Lesbos, la règle F a été généralisée à tous les mots (excepté seulement les proclitiques qui ne peuvent pas porter du tout d'accent inhérent). Cela revient à dire qu'aucun mot n'a plus à être marqué comme une exception à la règle F. [p. 76] F. new_statements.translation: [p. 81] We know, from the explicit testimony of the Greek grammarians, that Doric did not have rule G'; the forms there are of the type παιδῶν and not, as in Attic, παίδων. [...] And since Aeolic had generalized rule F (recessive accent), only Attic can have had rule G'. [p. 90] Thus, in the dialect of Lesbos, rule F was generalized to all words (except only the proclitics, which cannot carry any inherent accent at all). This amounts to saying that no word any longer has to be marked as an exception to rule F. [p. 76] F. V -> 'V / __ C0V0C0VC0 #, where C0V0C0VC0 # is the 'final ensemble' of Jakobson (1937) and Kurylowicz (1958).

new_statements.relation_note: The catalog codes Ancient North Greek 'tonal' from Smyth 1920 (musical/pitch accent, no accent farther back than the antepenult) with an empty rule. Kiparsky's analysis is the same prosodic type (pitch accent on morae within the final window) and adds placement facts for the dialects anci1249 groups: Lesbian Aeolic generalized the recessive accent to all non-proclitic words (position predictable), and Doric lacked the Attic retraction G' (παιδῶν, διετής vs Attic παίδων, διέτης). This supersedes the compilers 'adds no statement about this variety', which rested on the landing-page abstract only; the dialect statements are in the body (pp. 81, 90). No placement or type conflict with the catal…
new_statements.rule_in_words: Greek accent is analysed as a mora-borne (pitch) accent: long vowels are two morae, circumflex = accent on the first mora, acute = accent on the second, with a redundant falling contour on post-tonic morae, and all accent shifts move leftward; a recessive rule F puts the accent as far from the word end as the 'final ensemble' (law of limitation) allows. For the varieties grouped under anci1249: in Lesbian (Aeolic) rule F was generalized to every word except proclitics, so accent position is fully predictable and recessive (as far back as the limitation permits, i.e. depending on the quantity of the final syllable); Doric (and 'non-Attic' generally) lacked the Attic iambic retraction G', keeping inherited final accents of the type παιδῶν, διετής where Attic has παίδων, διέτης.
new_statements.secondary_stress: None described as such; p. 75-76 posits a redundant [+accentue] falling contour on the morae after the main accent (compared to the Sanskrit svarita), which is a pitch contour, not a secondary stress.
new_statements.exceptions: Lesbian: proclitics cannot bear an inherent accent and are the only words outside the generalized recessive rule (p. 90). Attic-internal: rule G and Wheeler's Law have lexical exceptions (ἡγεμών, γενεά, ἐχῖνος; suffix -ικός undergoes neither, p. 80 n. 5); Homeric ἔγωγε, θυγάτηρ are called atticisms (p. 81).
new_statements.identity_note: The article's synchronic rule system is built for Classical Attic declension; its statements bearing on anci1249 concern Lesbian (the dialect of Lesbos, Aeolic: generalized recessive accent, pp. 81, 90) and Doric / 'non-Attic' (no iambic retraction G', p. 81). Thessalian, Boeotian and Northwest Greek are not treated individually.

tone_statements.citation: Chadwick, John. 1992. The Thessalian Accent. Glotta 70(1/2): 2-14. Goettingen: Vandenhoeck & Ruprecht.
tone_statements.quote: daß die Dorier den Akut auf die letzte Silbe ziehen und in dieser Silbe den Akut an Stelle des Circumflex lieben, auf ein besonderes Akzentgesetz hinzu- weisen, das sich so formulieren läßt: der Akzent ist um eine More oder Quantitätseinheit nach dem Ende zu verschoben.
tone_statements.translation: [the grammarians' remark] that the Dorians draw the acute onto the last syllable and in that syllable favour the acute in place of the circumflex seems to point to a special accent law, which can be formulated thus: the accent is shifted by one mora or unit of quantity toward the end [of the word].

tone_statements.quote: Die Gelehrten des hellenistischen Zeitalters haben an dem Lesbischen ihrer Zeit beobachtet, daß der Accent in allen Wörtern außer den Präpositionen und Conjunctionen so weit wie möglich vom Wortende zurückgezogen wird. Die Erscheinung ist unter dem Namen der äolischen Baiytonese bekannt.
tone_statements.translation: The scholars of the Hellenistic age observed in the Lesbian of their time that the accent is drawn back as far as possible from the end of the word in all words except prepositions and conjunctions. The phenomenon is known under the name of Aeolic barytonesis. ('Baiytonese' is the scanned's rendering of 'Barytonese'.)
tone_statements.locator: Bd. I, Der lesbische Dialekt, 'I Betonung' sect. 1-2, pp. 7-9 (quote p. 7); Bd. I Vorwort (Boeotian accent paragraph only); Bd. II Vorwort (Doric accent omitted)

tone_statements.translation: it emerges from this collection that only the prepositions and conjunctions resisted the retraction of the accent. In all other words the accent moved as far away from the end of the word as possible

tone_statements.quote: (1) and (2) may occur in languages or dialects which have not a word-initial stress, but a non initial tonal accent, namely Mycenaean and Lesbian, also Boeotian. In these dialects the position of the accent is conditioned by the quantity of the last syllable: in Lesbian, the tonal accent shifts to the leftmost position as allowed by the last syllable restriction rule (barytonesis). … Accordingly we can assume by implication the existence of a word-initial stress accent in Thessalian.
tone_statements.locator: p. 132, end of sect. 12 and sect. 13
tone_statements.summary: Lesbian and Boeotian have a tonal (pitch) accent whose position depends on final-syllable quantity, recessive in Lesbian; Thessalian is argued to have had a word-initial stress accent instead.

tone_statements.quote: das im Attischen durchgeführte Gesetz, nach dem die betonte von xXatur lange paeuültima bei kurzer ultima nur den Circumflex haben darf, im Dorischen nicht bestand … der als tövog wvöihoc erscheinende Acutauf der paenultima auch bei kurzer ultima bestehen bleiben konnte … wenn die Dorier wirklich bei Betonun- einer langen Silbe den Accent stets auf die zweite Moni gelegt hätten, der Circuniflox niemals von Ihnen hätte gebraucht werden können. Und für seine Existenz im dorischen Dialekt debt es doch Zeugnisse … in Hülle und Fülle.
tone_statements.translation: the law carried through in Attic, by which an accented naturally long penult before a short ultima may bear only the circumflex, did not hold in Doric ... [rather] the acute, appearing as [tonos ..., Greek garbled], could remain on the penult even before a short ultima ... if the Dorians, in accenting a long syllable, had really always put the accent on the second mora, the circumflex could never have been used by them. And for its existence in the Doric dialect there is evidence ... in abundance.
tone_statements.locator: Part I 'Bemerkungen zur dorischen Accentuation', p. 1 (opening thesis) and p. 5, section 4 (rebuttal of Cauer)
tone_statements.summary: Doric Greek accent in the acute/circumflex/grave framework, placed by syllable and mora; unlike Attic, Doric allowed an acute on a long penult before a short ultima (no forced properispomena).

tone.translation: the law carried through in Attic, by which an accented naturally long penult before a short ultima may bear only the circumflex, did not hold in Doric ... [rather] the acute, appearing as [tonos ..., Greek garbled], could remain on the penult even before a short ultima ... if the Dorians, in accenting a long syllable, had really always put the accent on the second mora, the circumflex could never have been used by them. And for its existence in the Doric dialect there is evidence ... in abundance.

tone.quote: Doric accentuation is a particular kind of orthography which concerned Doric—or purported Doric—ancient Greek authors … this particular kind of accentuation is internally consistent: in the cases mentioned in the grammatical tradition, the accent, in comparison to the corresponding Attic forms, is constantly a mora closer to the word end. … a word which in Attic is proparoxytone, in Doric is paroxytone (ἀγγέλοι, τυπτομένοι … ); if in Attic a word is paroxytone, in Doric it is perispomenon (τουτῶν, ἀλλῶν, παιδῶν … )
